title: Jack Ruby in the 1963 JFK Release Series
metaDescription: Dallas nightclub operator Jack Ruby fatally shot Lee Harvey Oswald on Nov. 24, 1963. FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby recur in JFK releases.
h1: Jack Ruby in FBI and Warren Commission interviews
lede: Dallas nightclub operator Jack Ruby fatally shot Lee Harvey Oswald in the Dallas police basement on November 24, 1963. FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appear repeatedly in the JFK release series. BlackVaultDocs’ figure hub matches the name Jack Ruby in document titles from public NARA releases. The hub is a title index, not a biography of motive and not a file count. PDFs remain on the originating archive.

sections.h2: What the Ruby figure hub lists
paragraphs: The figure slug jack-ruby groups indexed titles that name Jack Ruby. The packet supplies no document count, so this page does not invent one. The public-record identity in the blurb is specific: Dallas nightclub operator; fatally shot Lee Harvey Oswald in the Dallas police basement on November 24, 1963; FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appear repeatedly in the JFK release series.

A title that names Ruby is a catalog hit. It is not a finding that every page of the file is “about” Ruby. Interviews of associates appear in the same blurb as interviews of Ruby himself. This overlay does not split those two classes of interview, because the packet does not give separate counts.

Lee Harvey Oswald is named in the blurb as the man Ruby shot on November 24, 1963. Oswald has a separate figure hub. This page does not merge the two name indexes. The related topic link on the packet is the JFK assassination collection.

November 24, 1963 is the date in the packet for the shooting in the Dallas police basement. The blurb does not give a trial date or a death date for Ruby. This page therefore does not add them. What it can repeat is that FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appear repeatedly in the JFK release series.

“Appear repeatedly” is a qualitative statement in the blurb, not a number. This overlay does not convert it into a count of interviews or a count of associates. Researchers who need the transcripts should open the originating archive from the figure hub. BlackVaultDocs matches names in titles; it does not re-host the PDFs.

sections.h2: How name matching works for Ruby
paragraphs: Figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. The Ruby hub is that match, not a complete FOIA log and not a Dallas police file dump. A missing title hit means the indexed title in this ingest did not match the name as implemented, not that NARA never held an interview.
The all-figures directory lists other people in the same name index. Use the Ruby hub for titles that name him; use the JFK assassination collection for the broader posting named on this packet.

sections.h2: What this page does not claim
paragraphs: This overlay does not argue why Ruby shot Oswald, whether others were involved, or what the interviews “really show.” It restates the packet: Dallas nightclub operator; fatal shooting of Lee Harvey Oswald in the Dallas police basement on November 24, 1963; FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appearing repeatedly in the JFK release series. Conspiracy commentary is outside the index.
No NARA ID is in the facts. No document total is in the facts. Cite the November 24, 1963 date and the named interview series. Do not attach an invented file count to Ruby’s name.

The Jack Ruby figure hub is the live title list. All figures shows the rest of the name index. The JFK assassination collection is the related topic link on this packet. Open the originating archive for scans. A later ingest can retag titles; this prose still will not invent a document count for Ruby.

Interviews of Ruby and interviews of his associates are named together in the blurb. This page does not split them. A title that names an associate without naming Ruby would not be promised by this name index. Open the originating archive for the scan behind any title that does match.

sections.h2: How to cite Jack Ruby on this site
paragraphs: Cite Jack Ruby as the Dallas nightclub operator who fatally shot Lee Harvey Oswald in the Dallas police basement on November 24, 1963, with FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appearing repeatedly in the JFK release series, as matched by name in indexed titles on BlackVaultDocs. Do not cite a document count from this guide. Do not treat the figure hub as a finding on motive or conspiracy. The source note is that figure hubs match names in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs.

November 24, 1963 is the only date this packet gives for the shooting. The Dallas police basement is the only place it gives. Cite those facts with the FBI and Warren Commission interview series. Do not add a trial date from outside the facts.

faqs.q: Who was Jack Ruby in the JFK declassified files?
faqs.a: The packet identifies Jack Ruby as a Dallas nightclub operator who fatally shot Lee Harvey Oswald in the Dallas police basement on November 24, 1963. FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appear repeatedly in the JFK release series. BlackVaultDocs matches the name in indexed titles. This page does not assign a file count.

faqs.q: When did Jack Ruby shoot Lee Harvey Oswald?
faqs.a: The blurb dates the shooting to November 24, 1963, in the Dallas police basement. That is the chronology this page cites. The packet does not give a document count for that date. Titles that name Ruby appear on the figure hub; PDFs remain on the originating archive.

faqs.q: Which interviews of Jack Ruby are in the JFK release series?
faqs.a: The blurb states that FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appear repeatedly in the JFK release series. It does not number those interviews or list associate names. This page does not invent those splits. Open the figure hub and the originating archive for the scans.

faqs.q: Does the Ruby figure hub prove a conspiracy?
faqs.a: No. The hub matches the name Jack Ruby in document titles from public NARA releases indexed on BlackVaultDocs. It restates the November 24, 1963 shooting of Lee Harvey Oswald and the presence of FBI and Warren Commission interviews. It does not interpret those interviews as proof of a plot.

takeaways: Jack Ruby was a Dallas nightclub operator who fatally shot Lee Harvey Oswald on November 24, 1963.
The shooting took place in the Dallas police basement.
FBI and Warren Commission interviews of Ruby and his associates appear repeatedly in the JFK release series.
The figure hub matches that name in indexed titles; this packet supplies no document count.
This page does not treat title hits as a finding on motive or conspiracy.
